summary: Lille's parking story is one of progressive tightening: the 2018 decriminalisation gave the city control of on-street charges, followed by a 2022 plan to extend paid parking to nearly all districts, new zoned tariffs and higher FPS from April 2023, and the pedestrianisation of the Grand'Place in January 2026. At metropolitan level the Plan de Mobilité (October 2023) and PLU3 (June 2024) cap parking supply, while the ZFE (since January 2025) bans only unclassified vehicles and its national abolition was struck down by the Conseil constitutionnel in May 2026. Off-street supply is run by concession holders (Indigo, Effia, SORELI, SEM Ville Renouvelée) and ilévia for park-and-ride, with the MEL counting about 19,600 city-centre and 5,500 park-and-ride spaces and Lille car parks priced well above Roubaix and Tourcoing. In June 2026 the council under mayor Arnaud Deslandes cut resident parking subscriptions to €1 a year for low-income households from September 2026, and Braderie weekend shows the event-driven demand handled by closing central car parks and pushing park-and-ride.

items.text: France's 2018 on-street parking reform (MAPTAM law, in force 2018) decriminalised paid street parking: users pay a fee for use of the public domain and, if they do not pay properly, a post-parking charge (FPS) set by each local authority, replacing the former national fine of €17. In Lille the city runs on-street parking directly (en régie), unlike Roubaix, which delegated it to a SEM.
items.source_title: Cahier du stationnement métropolitain 2024 (ADULM / Métropole Européenne de Lille, November 2024)

items.text: On 30 September 2022 Lille's municipal council adopted a plan to extend paid on-street parking progressively, up to 2025, to almost the whole city. Moulins was already paid from February 2024 and Fives and Saint-Maurice-Pellevoisin were planned for end 2024; only Lille-Sud and Faubourg de Béthune kept free street parking at the time of the report. Stated aims were decluttering public space, tackling long-stay 'ventouse' cars and improving turnover.
items.source_title: Cahier du stationnement métropolitain 2024 (ADULM / Métropole Européenne de Lille, November 2024)

items.text: Lille council approved paid parking for six more districts: Vauban-Esquermes and Wazemmes in early 2023, then Bois-Blancs, Fives, Moulins and Saint-Maurice-Pellevoisin in 2024. Paid hours are 9:00 to 19:00 except Sundays and public holidays; Lille-Sud and Faubourg-de-Béthune stay free. The article presents the extension as part of the metropolitan mobility plan.
items.source_title: Lille : le stationnement deviendra payant dans six quartiers d'ici 2024 - ICI

items.text: A new Lille on-street parking tariff grid took effect on 3 April 2023, with higher prices in all zones. The FPS (post-parking charge) rose from €17 to €35 in the city centre and €25 in other zones. The city said the aim was to reduce vehicles in town and ensure better rotation, targeting 'ventouse' cars while encouraging short stays.
items.source_title: Stationnement : se garer coûte plus cher désormais à Lille depuis début avril - ICI

items.text: Paid on-street parking was extended to two more Lille districts, Vauban-Esquermes and Wazemmes, from 1 June 2023. Resident subscriptions were offered at three income-based levels (€10, €15 and the full €25 rate, per the city's grid).
items.source_title: [Stationnement à Lille] Les nouveaux tarifs et les nouveaux quartiers payants au 1er juin 2023 - Zoom Sur Lille

items.text: Lille's on-street parking is split into zones: orange (hypercentre, first 30 minutes free, no resident parking), yellow (wider centre incl. Vieux-Lille, Saint-Sauveur, rue Solférino), green (newly paid residential districts and Bois-Blancs, free on Saturday) and azur (shopping streets within the green zone, 30 minutes free). Resident subscriptions moved from a single €25 per month to three income-based levels (€10, €15, €25), and the FPS rose from €17 to €25 (azur/green) or €35 (orange/yellow).
items.source_title: Cahier du stationnement métropolitain 2024 (ADULM / Métropole Européenne de Lille, November 2024)

items.text: On 19 June 2026 Lille's municipal council (mayor Arnaud Deslandes) adopted a purchasing-power package that includes cutting the annual resident parking subscription to €1 for lower-income households from 1 September 2026, based on family-quotient thresholds.
items.source_title: Lille : cinq mesures pour le pouvoir d'achat adoptées par le conseil municipal

items.text: The Métropole Européenne de Lille adopted its Plan de Mobilité (PDM), horizon 2035, at the metropolitan council of 20 October 2023. It replaces the previous urban travel plan and is based on three axes (infrastructure, services, behaviours) with 52 actions.
items.source_title: Plan de mobilité

items.text: The PDM treats parking as a central tool and recommends to 'maîtriser, optimiser et réglementer' supply: ceilings on parking in new offices, lower minimum norms for housing in well-served areas, regulation extended around high-quality public transport stops, and more relay parking upstream of dense areas. The PLU3, approved June 2024, translates this into parking norms, including a dedicated hyper-central Lille sector (S0.1).
items.source_title: Cahier du stationnement métropolitain 2024 (ADULM / Métropole Européenne de Lille, November 2024)

items.text: The MEL low-emission zone (ZFE-m) was set to start on 1 January 2025 across all 95 communes, for three years (to 31 December 2027). Only vehicles classed 'non classés' under Crit'Air (roughly pre-1997 registrations) are banned 24/7; the Crit'Air sticker must be displayed to circulate in the zone.
items.source_title: Dossier Zone à Faible Émission MEL (PDF, lillemetropole.fr, December 2024)

items.text: MEL chose a minimal ZFE scenario in October 2024: only 'non classés' vehicles (about 6,290 across the 95 communes) were targeted. Of 95 communes consulted, 38 opposed a stricter scenario, 33 supported it, 9 abstained and 15 did not respond.
items.source_title: Pollution : la métropole lilloise opte pour une ZFE… minimaliste

items.text: On 15 April 2026 Parliament adopted the 'simplification of economic life' bill, which included abolishing low-emission zones; the MEL zone, in force since 1 January 2025, was the only ZFE in Hauts-de-France.
items.source_title: ZFE : un dispositif qui a eu du mal à se mettre en place dans le Nord et le Pas-de-Calais - ICI

items.text: On 21 May 2026 the Conseil constitutionnel (decision 2026-903 DC) struck down the article abolishing ZFEs as a legislative rider unrelated to the bill, on procedural grounds; the framework for low-emission zones therefore remained legally intact.
items.source_title: Suppression de la ZFE : pourquoi le Conseil constitutionnel a retoqué la mesure ?

items.text: Lille's Grand'Place (place du Général de Gaulle) became fully pedestrian on 12 January 2026, with 500 bollards removed from the vehicle lane. The underground car park of about 300 spaces stays open via rue Nationale; the city notes about ten car parks within a 10-minute walk. Deliveries are allowed 7:00 to 11:00.
items.source_title: “C’est le sens de l’histoire” : la Grand’Place, cœur battant de Lille, devient 100% piétonne

items.text: Zoom Sur Lille, summarising the city's information, reported that around the pedestrianised Grand'Place there are 7,500 spaces in 10 car parks within a 10-minute walk, plus 592 on-street spaces. The pedestrian area also covers rue Pierre-Mauroy, rue Esquermoise and rue du Curé-Saint-Étienne.
items.source_title: La Grand'Place de Lille est piétonne de façon permanente depuis le 12 janvier 2026 - Zoom Sur Lille

items.text: Braderie de Lille, 5-6 September 2026: about 2.5 million visitors expected. Central access was banned from Friday 4 September 7 p.m. to Monday 7 September 1 a.m., downtown car parks close from 4 September 7 p.m. to 7 September 6 a.m., and 13 free park-and-ride sites (42 to 2,041 spaces) were offered; metro and tram ran 24 hours.
items.source_title: CARTE - Braderie de Lille 2026 : accès, circulation et stationnement, tout ce qu'il faut savoir pour venir chiner - ICI

items.text: Between the 1998 and 2016 household travel surveys the MEL car fleet grew from 457,000 to 530,000 cars (+16%), and in 2016 cars accounted for 2.4 million of 4.2 million daily trips (57.5%). The report says that where parking is restricted or priced the car share falls by nearly 20 points in well-served areas with tram or metro.
items.source_title: Cahier du stationnement métropolitain 2024 (ADULM / Métropole Européenne de Lille, November 2024)

items.text: MEL counted more than one million parking spaces: about 330,000 public and 700,000 private. It identified 47 access-controlled car parks open to the public (city-centre car parks and park-and-ride); the city-centre car parks total 19,561 spaces and the P+R 5,526 (including 300 temporary spaces during works at Saint-Philibert).
items.source_title: Cahier du stationnement métropolitain 2024 (ADULM / Métropole Européenne de Lille, November 2024)

items.text: Access-controlled public car parks are mostly owned by MEL, but some are owned by the city of Lille (Grand Place and Vieux-Lille); none is run directly by MEL or the cities. They are operated under public-service concessions by private operators (Indigo, Effia) or semi-public firms (SEM Ville Renouvelée, SORELI), while park-and-ride sites are run by Ilevia. The privately owned Tanneurs shopping-centre car park is run by Indigo.
items.source_title: Cahier du stationnement métropolitain 2024 (ADULM / Métropole Européenne de Lille, November 2024)

items.text: A 2023 ADULM comparison found Lille car parks cost on average 1.5 times more than Roubaix/Tourcoing from the first half hour and 2 times more from one hour, with an average monthly subscription of €134 in Lille against €40 (Roubaix) and €44 (Tourcoing). Effia-concession car parks (République, Opéra, Nouveau Siècle) were the cheapest of the public ones; Indigo's Euralille Gare A and Gare B were the dearest for long stays; the Tanneurs car park was the dearest up to the 10th hour.
items.source_title: Cahier du stationnement métropolitain 2024 (ADULM / Métropole Européenne de Lille, November 2024)

items.text: Lille's opposition group Faire Respirer (statement by Violette Spillebout, council of 10 October 2025) said Indigo operates the city-owned Grand'Place car park under a 50-year concession to 2049, with the city receiving 7% of turnover (€218,000 of €3.02 million in 2024) and a rate of €2.80 per hour. This is an opposition group's claim, not an official figure.
items.source_title: Parking Grand'Place - FAIRE RESPIRER

items.text: Indigo Neo's page for Euralille Centre Commercial (open 24/7, automatic plate recognition) showed indicative rates for 7 October 2026 of €1.70 for 30 minutes and €2.40 for 1 hour. Its Euralille Gare A (Europe) page showed €1.90 for 30 minutes and €2.70 for 1 hour. The page states only tariffs posted at the entrance apply.
items.source_title: Euralille Centre Commercial Parking - INDIGO Neo

items.text: Indigo Neo's page for the Les Tanneurs car park (70 rue du Molinel, open 24/7, EV charging station, plate recognition) showed hourly rates of €1.60 for 30 minutes and €3.20 for 1 hour when opened in October 2026.
items.source_title: Parking Les Tanneurs, Lille - INDIGO Neo

items.text: Effia's page for Parking Lille Nouveau Siècle (19 place Mendès France, open 24/7) listed rates of €2.10 for 1 hour, €5.70 for 3 hours and €17.00 for 24 hours, a €3.20 evening rate (7 p.m.-1 a.m.) and a €108 monthly subscription when opened in October 2026.
items.source_title: Parking Lille Nouveau Siècle - EFFIA

items.text: The Saint-Philibert park-and-ride in Lomme (near Saint-Philibert metro station) is being rebuilt and extended from 335 to about 570 spaces, in a ten-half-level building with photovoltaic panels, works having started in September 2023, with commissioning announced for 6 September. Entry is free but exit requires validation of an ilévia or TER same-day ticket. The page is dated 4 June 2025.
items.source_title: Lomme : le parking P+R Saint-Philibert double sa capacité

items.text: MEL's Iléwatt public EV charging service, launched in July 2024, is to reach nearly 900 charging points at nearly 300 locations. It covers 12 park-and-ride sites and 25 downtown car parks in Lille, Roubaix and Tourcoing, where prices vary by operator (e.g. Effia €0.40/kWh plus €1.50 access fee; INDIGO Neo €0.29/kWh for subscribers, €0.45/kWh occasional).
items.source_title: Métropole Européenne de Lille - Grands projets - Bornes de recharge électrique

items.text: In June 2021 MEL announced a plan to move from about 50 public charging points to over 4,000 within four years through a service concession, including 800 equipped spaces in city-centre car parks and 300 in park-and-ride sites by 2025.
items.source_title: La Métropole Européenne de Lille équipe massivement le territoire de bornes de recharge pour accompagner le développement rapide de l'électromobilité

items.text: MEL and ilévia announced new 52-metre trains on metro line 1 (testing from 21 September 2025, with works and interruptions to 28 October 2025) with full commercial service planned for February 2026, to increase line capacity.
items.source_title: Travaux - Doublement des rames de métro de la ligne 1
